chunks: He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad reported to me, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Hasani, who reported from Abu Musa Isa ibn Mahran, who reported from Abu Yashkur al-Balkhi, who reported from Musa ibn Ubaidah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Awf ibn Malik, who said:

The Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said one day: "How I wish to meet my brothers!" So Abu Bakr and Umar said to him: "Are we not your brothers? We have believed in you and migrated with you."
He, peace be upon him and his family, said: "You have believed and you have migrated, yet how I wish to meet my brothers." They repeated the statement.

Then the Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said: "You are my companions, but my brothers are those who will come after you. They will believe in me, love me, help me, and confirm me - without ever having seen me. How I wish to meet my brothers!"

key_terms.أصحابي: My companions - those who physically accompanied the Prophet during his lifetime
key_terms.إخواني: My brothers - used by the Prophet to refer to future believers who would accept Islam without seeing him
key_terms.هاجرنا: We migrated - referring to the Hijra, the migration from Mecca to Medina

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about future believers who never saw him?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) expressed deep longing for future believers whom he called "brothers" - people who would believe in him, love him, and support his message without ever meeting him in person. He distinguished them from his companions (sahaba) who witnessed him directly, indicating that faith without physical witness carries special merit. This hadith, narrated by the companion Awf ibn Malik, was spoken in the presence of Abu Bakr and Umar who questioned whether they were not his brothers.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 9. He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad reported to me from Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Hasani who reported from Abu Musa Isa ibn Mahran, who reported from Abu Yashkur al-Balkhi, who reported from Musa ibn Ubaidah, from Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurzi, from Awf ibn Malik, that:
The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, once said: "How eager am I to meet my brothers." So Abu Bakr and Umar said: "Are we not your brothers? We have believed in you, and migrated with you."
The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: "No doubt, you have believed and migrated, yet I am eager to meet my brothers." Then he repeated the statement.

Then he said: "You are my companions. But my brothers are those who will come after you have gone. They will believe in me, love me, help me, and confirm me - without ever having seen me. How I wish to meet my brothers!"
